facts.claim: Table 0 is sheet 'Report' in report.xlsx and is the only visible sheet; it has 18 rows and 4 columns.
Cell A1 holds the title 'Inventory and price list'.
Cell A2 states 'Currency: EUR; price per individual piece; stock below is in pieces.', establishing the currency and piece basis for all product rows.
Row 4 holds section/group labels ('Identity' in A4, 'Commercial' in C4), while row 5 holds the actual column names: SKU (A5), Product name (B5), Selling price (C5), Stock pieces (D5).
Rows 6-17 contain 12 product-level data rows; each row has one SKU, one product name, one selling price, and one stock-pieces value.
Row 18 is a TOTAL row: A18='TOTAL', B18 is blank, C18=1926, D18=234; it is not a product record.
SKUs in A6:A17 are six-digit strings from '000001' through '000012'; they carry leading zeros.
SKUs are unique across the 12 product rows; the column profile reports 12 distinct non-null values and unique_ratio 1.0.
Product name values in B6:B17 are non-null and distinct across the 12 rows, for example 'Coffee variant 01' and 'Shampoo variant 02'.
Selling price values in C6:C17 are integer numbers from 67 to 254; the raw cells contain no currency symbols or decimal separators.
Stock pieces values in D6:D17 are integer numbers from 3 to 36.
Column D is explicitly labeled 'Stock pieces' (D5) and A2 says stock below is in pieces, so no pack-size conversion is stated by the source.
The table profile reports a constant observed ratio of 3.0 between 'Stock pieces' and numeric SKU across 12 compared rows; this is an observed association, not a stated business rule.
The Report sheet has zero formula cells, zero error cells, zero hidden rows, and zero hidden columns in the workbook profile.

hypotheses: The profile's header_row=4 likely reflects the merged section-label row; raw cell inspection shows the field-name header is row 5.
The perfect sequence stock=3*SKU-number appears to be a constructed sample pattern rather than an ERP stock rule.
C18=1926 and D18=234 look like arithmetic totals of the 12 rows, but the workbook has no formulas to confirm how they were produced.
mapping_guidance: Map the master product population from rows 6-17 only (12 rows); exclude row 18.
Set sku from A6:A17 as a string, preserving the six leading-zero digits exactly.
Set product_name directly from B6:B17 without deriving names from SKU or pattern.
Set price from C6:C17 as a JSON number using the stored integer amount; do not add currency symbols or rescale.
Set currency to 'EUR' for every record from the sheet-level statement in A2; do not infer currency from numeric shape.
Set qty from D6:D17 as a JSON number in pieces, matching the D5 header and A2 piece-basis note.
Use row 5 as the column-header row; row 4 is a group/section header and should not be treated as field names.
Do not use the observed SKU-to-stock ratio of 3.0 to compute qty; qty is present directly in D.
Do not use C18 or D18 as product values or totals in output.
All 12 data rows have non-null values for all four source fields, so required target fields can be populated without null fallbacks in this file.
Emit only the target fields allowed by the schema (sku, product_name, price, currency, qty) because additionalProperties is false.
Do not invent tax, locale, pack size, or rounding rules not stated in the source.
missing_information: No cell states whether selling prices are tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive; the target asks only for a price amount, so no tax field should be invented.
No per-row currency column exists; the only currency evidence is the sheet-level note in A2.
No source statement defines pack size or unit conversions beyond the piece basis stated in A2 and D5.
